notes: This is narrower than the legacy no-in-process-call pressure: retained typed sessions already pass. It tracks authoritative admission of a provider selected at runtime, not generic dynamic linking or arbitrary code loading.

reproducer.actual: native/mncs/actions/family/v1.mncs imports mncs.test.provider.v2 and calls provider_v2.run_selected_batch directly. The Phase VI provider canary refuses a mismatched interface descriptor, but only for a statically linked application descriptor.
reproducer.expected: Actions selects a provider only from authoritative family/provider declaration facts, and the runtime admits the exact descriptor/source/interface/revision before the same-session typed call.
reproducer.hostLocus: mncs-actions/native/mncs/actions/family/v1.mncs and the generic mncs run-app admission boundary

requiredBehavior: Given a Commons-selected ProviderDeclaration, the generic runtime must admit the declared provider into the consumer session, establish descriptor/content/source/interface/revision identities from trusted admitted material, refuse mismatches, and return a typed callable boundary without a provider-specific Actions import or subprocess semantic adapter.

signals.threatModel: checked repository/source and content identity; no signing guarantee claimed

summary: A native consumer can make a same-session typed provider call, but the current Actions path can only establish provider identity by statically importing mncs-test provider v2. A supplied descriptor is not yet an authoritative runtime selection and admission mechanism.
title: Native consumers lack authoritative provider descriptor admission
